Package hadur2.core.gun

Class ShadowAim

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.gun.ShadowAim
public final class ShadowAim extends Object
GUN-7: bullets are armour. Given the angle the chosen gun would fire along, it weighs a small set of nearby candidate angles by the damage a hit would do plus the damage the bullet's shadows would save us, and fires the best.

The value of a candidate a is P(hit at a) * damage(power) + ShadowValue.avoided(a, power): the first term is the gun's probability mass at the angle (see ShadowAim.Mass) times Robocode's damage for the power, the second is what the duel says the bullet's path blocks on the intervals movement published (MOVE-8). The gun's own angle comes first and wins every tie, so with nothing to shadow the choice is the gun's, exactly.

Candidates, all bounded: the gun's angle; four offsets of +-0.45 and +-0.9 of the target's half-width, so the bullet still hits where the gun's mass is but its path crosses other enemy bullets; and, when the gun is the main gun, up to MAX_SAMPLES of its neighbours' own angles within two half-widths of its choice (a kernel sample is an angle the gun believes in). The other virtual guns' angles are not candidates: they are computed only when a real bullet leaves, and the KNN searches are the gun's costly part.

    ShadowAim.Mass
    The gun's probability mass over firing angles: a Gaussian kernel density of points (the main gun's neighbours, or one point at the gun's angle), each weight strong, of bandwidth bandwidth, scaled so that the value is the chance a bullet fired along the angle hits.

    • choose

      public static double choose(double gunAngle, ShadowAim.Mass mass, double halfWidth, double power, ShadowValue shadow)
      The firing angle GUN-7 picks.
      Parameters:
      gunAngle - the angle the chosen gun would fire along, absolute radians
      mass - the gun's probability mass over angles
      halfWidth - the target's angular half-width at this range, radians
      power - the bullet's power
      shadow - the damage-avoided term; when not ShadowValue.active() the answer is gunAngle itself
      Returns:
      an absolute bearing in [0, 2pi)

    • pick

      static int pick(double[] angles, double[] hits, int n, double power, ShadowValue shadow)
      The index of the candidate with the greatest value, hit * damage + avoided; the lowest index on a tie, so the gun's own angle (index 0) is kept unless another is strictly better.
      Parameters:
      angles - the candidates' angles, absolute radians
      hits - each candidate's chance of hitting
      n - how many of them to consider
      power - the bullet's power
      shadow - the damage-avoided term
      Returns:
      an index in [0, n)
